iut_type: End Product (Topre device), Bluetooth module change and Core Specification version decision
customer_question: Our Bluetooth module is changing from a Taiyo Yuden part to a Kaga FEI part (QDID:97470). If we keep our registration at the existing Core Specification 4.2, do we need to do anything? If we instead want to move up to 5.0, is testing required, or just a new application? And does re-applying for 5.0 without any other changes require a new test sample?
question_variants: Does a module vendor change require any registration action if staying on the same Core Spec version?
Does upgrading to Core Spec 5.0 require new testing, or can existing test reports be reused?
actual_issue: The customer was changing their Bluetooth module supplier and needed to understand the registration implications both for staying on their current Core Specification version and for potentially upgrading to a newer one, including whether new testing or sample submission would be required either way.
plain_english_explanation: If the customer keeps their registration at the existing Core Specification version (4.2) despite the module vendor change, no procedural action is needed at all. If instead they want to move up to Core Specification 5.0, no new testing is required — the existing test reports from the prior registration can be reused — but a new registration (with its own $11,040 application fee) is still required, since this is treated as a distinct registration rather than a modification of the existing one. Because the change is application-only (reusing existing test data), no new test sample needs to be prepared or submitted for this 5.0 upgrade.
consultant_answer: If you stay at Core Specification 4.2 despite the module vendor change, no action is needed at all. If you want to move up to Core Specification 5.0, no new testing is required — your existing test reports can be reused — but a new registration (with its own $11,040 application fee) is still required, since this is a distinct registration rather than a modification of your existing one. Since this is application-only, no new test sample needs to be prepared.
decision_logic: A Core Specification version upgrade can be achieved purely through a new registration application reusing existing test reports, without new testing, as long as the underlying product hasn't changed in ways that would invalidate those existing results — staying on the current version requires no action at all regardless of an unrelated module vendor change.
final_recommendation: When a customer asks about upgrading Core Specification version alongside an unrelated component change, clearly separate the 'stay at current version' (no action) and 'upgrade version' (new application, reused test data, no new testing) paths so they can make an informed cost/benefit decision.
risk_if_done_wrong: A customer assuming a Core Spec version upgrade requires full retesting might either avoid a beneficial upgrade unnecessarily, or might fail to budget for the still-required new registration application fee, assuming no cost was involved at all.
